Yeah, I've run into similar frustrations, but I see why they made the choice they did. The options for a charging port location would be

the top (would require the switch be placed into dock upside down, which with how the joycons are removed, would be a major PITA. It would also render the 3.5 mil port unusuable while the switch is docked, though they could have added a 3.5 mil port to the dock).

The back (would make sliding the switch into the dock difficult to design. Only thing I can think of would be a retractable connector inside the dock itself that engages based off a button being depressed by the switch, which would be fragile, and make the dock MUCH thicker)

the side (would make it impossible to create the dock with open sides, which would make the joycons unchargeable, And, I just realized, would make the device unchargeable entirely in handheld mode)

and the bottom, which is the only sensible one for dealing with the dock, BUT does make it impossible to use a charger with the kickstand.

Or they could have put in two ports, which is a significant expense for something that they were trying to make at as low a cost as possible to provide

This issue can be bypassed by the user by not using the kickstand, and instead placing it flat on the table when trying to charge. I could also see a cable that has a connector, then rigid plastic that matches the width and length of the bottom of the switch, then has the cable come out at a 90 degree angle working well, though it would be super ugly. Definitely something for third parties to solve. An exceedingly thin right angle connector could work as well, though I don't know if getting it to the required slimness is feasible without risking the plug breaking off inside the port
Or just put the port on top and let the display rotate...
which would be a pain in the ass in handheld mode. And require the additional hardware of an accelerometer in the switch itself, plus additional software development time to support that.
